# EXP-006 — general-model baseline and fallback evaluation preparation

**Preparation implemented. PAID EXPERIMENT NOT RUN.** No OpenAI inference endpoint was called, no validation predictions were generated by a general model, and actual experiment API spend this session is **$0**. All response/execution tests use clearly identified synthetic fixtures. EXP-001–005, their model code, dependencies, splits and results remain unchanged.

## Frozen candidate, prompt and settings

The candidate is **`gpt-6-luna`**, verified against the [official model page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-luna) on 2026-09-25. That page lists the alias but no dated snapshot. Every returned model ID must equal the requested ID or execution halts; an unchanged alias can still change underlying weights, so this is not immutable model pinning. Account access and live response compatibility remain untested.

The exact zero-shot instructions, containing all 77 official intent names in dataset order, are [prompt.txt](prompt.txt). The strict object schema is [schema.json](schema.json): one required `intent` field, restricted to those names, with no extra properties. Each independent request contains only that prompt, schema, settings, and one original customer message. No ground-truth label, specialist prediction/confidence, row ID, previous conversation, or example demonstration is sent. Dataset intent names are the class vocabulary, not request-specific ground truth. The prompt was frozen without general-model results; do not tune it on the evaluation.

[protocol.json](protocol.json) freezes Responses API, reasoning effort `none`, maximum 128 output tokens, Standard processing (`service_tier=default`), `store=false`, no streaming, disabled truncation, implicit cache mode/30-minute TTL, and no tools. Temperature/top-p are omitted and inherit provider defaults; deterministic generation is not promised. See [Responses reference](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/python/resources/responses/methods/create), [structured output](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs?api-mode=responses), and [GPT-6 settings](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model).

Protocol SHA-256: `d7f824ee761ca90d4dc3a848dd19e3928475c799d6713e03e336dc2a80c9ca68`.

## Data, execution and reuse

Read only the pinned source `train.csv`, official category mapping, existing v2 manifest, and versioned EXP-004/005 evidence. No split generation, specialist fitting, encoding, model deserialization, or official-test file access occurs. Training CSV checksum/positions are scanned mechanically; only the exact **770 existing validation texts and labels** are retained. Source labels for those rows are checked against archived truth; original train/validation IDs, normalized duplicates, stored sealed-test IDs/hashes, and all 15 primary record hashes are verified. No text inspection was used to write or tune the prompt.

One set of **770 unique API requests** supplies every comparison. With a maximum of two attempts per request, the ceiling is **1,540 attempts**, not 770 calls per specialist. All 15 EXP-004 primary specialists retain their EXP-005 acceptance prefixes: 0 (all fallback), 193, 385, 578, 693 and 770 accepted requests. The zero prefix is a reference, not a new threshold candidate. No acceptance set is optimized using general-model outcomes.

The cache key hashes the endpoint and complete request (input text, model, prompt, schema and generation settings). Saved request bodies and responses stay under ignored `artifacts/`; the same successful response is reused on resume and for all 90 specialist/coverage combinations. The manifest records IDs, protocol/data hashes, code revision/hashes, runtime and package versions. Every attempt retains its response body, returned model/tier, request ID, timestamps, wall time, usage, refusal/incomplete details, outcome and reserved cost. Request headers and API credentials are never logged. Cached files are checked before reuse; mock/live caches cannot mix.

Execution is serial with a process lock. Before any request, a durable attempt reservation and separate reservation ledger are saved. Interrupted/unknown attempts consume the attempt and budget allocation. Missing or truncated response files cannot reset that allocation. Network/timeout failures and HTTP 408/429/500/502/503/504 permit **one retry**, with the identical body and two-second delay; there are no SDK retries. Refusals, incomplete output, invalid labels/JSON, and ordinary valid answers are terminal. Wrong answers are never retried. Fatal HTTP configuration errors, model/tier drift or observed token/cost envelope breaches halt further requests and preserve evidence. Unobserved requests remain explicit failures in evaluation. Redirects and environment proxy overrides are disabled for the authenticated endpoint.

## Planned quality evaluation — not measured yet

Compute general-model accuracy and macro-F1 over **all 770 cases and 77 classes**, including unresolved cases as incorrect. Unknown outputs add false negatives to their true classes; they are not dropped or introduced as an extra macro class. Report status counts, unresolved counts, per-class precision/recall/F1, and the complete prediction set.

For each fixed accepted set, use the specialist on accepted IDs and that same general prediction set on rejected IDs. Compute combined accuracy and macro-F1 over all 770, plus fallback accuracy/error/unresolved counts on rejected requests alone. At 100% specialist coverage, fallback accuracy is undefined (`null`); at all fallback, combined metrics equal the standalone general model. Retain each of the 90 combinations and summarize the five specialist seeds with mean and sample SD. Five seeds reuse one validation dataset and one general-response set; they are not independent validation datasets or general-model replications. The fallback may be worse, including on rejected requests.

The **770 additional validation labels** remain part of the development-label budget; no new unique labels or demonstrations are added. This reused holdout supports exploratory comparison, not confirmatory production quality or threshold selection. Specialist inference has an unmeasured deployment cost, and no production latency measurement is planned here.

## Cost estimate and accounting

Official Standard prices per million tokens on 2026-09-25 are input **$0.10**, cached input **$0.01**, cache writes **$0.125**, and output **$0.50**. These assume short context (at most 272,000 input tokens), a nonregional endpoint and no separately priced tools. [Pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing), [cache accounting](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching).

The no-inference [dry run](dry_run.json) records each request's body hash, byte count and cost envelope:

| Planning scenario | USD |
| --- | ---: |
| Rough one-attempt estimate | 0.124057 |
| Conservative reservation, one attempt per request | 1.7313625 |
| Conservative reservation, two attempts per request | 3.462725 |
| Proposed spending cap, requiring future user approval | 4.00 |

The rough estimate uses `ceil(serialized request UTF-8 bytes / 4)` input tokens and 32 output tokens. The conservative envelope uses **2 × serialized bytes + 8,192 input tokens**, the full 128-output-token cap, and all input charged at the cache-write rate. It assumes **no cached-read discount**, including on retries. These are explicit token-count heuristics with large overhead, not server-verified token counts or guaranteed invoices. The local cap is enforced against this envelope before launch and before every attempt; it cannot guarantee third-party billing if prices or server token accounting violate the frozen assumptions. An observed breach stops further calls. Taxes, credits, account discounts and unrelated account usage are excluded.

Future actual experiment accounting totals usage-priced charges for all collection attempts, including failed/unknown attempts, separately from routed-workload estimates. With input `I`, cached reads `C`, writes `W`, output `O`, the frozen USD formula is `(0.10*(I-C-W) + 0.01*C + 0.125*W + 0.50*O)/1e6`. Reasoning tokens are recorded but already included in output billing. Missing usage/cache details remain unknown; retain reservations and report uncertainty instead of zero charges. If returned model/tier or observed usage invalidates pricing assumptions, no bounded exact-spend claim is made. Usage-priced cost is not invoice reconciliation.

Hypothetical routing replays recorded per-request usage/retries only for rejected IDs. It assumes the observed cache mix; routing order and traffic can change server cache behavior. A separate no-discount attempt envelope is available. This counterfactual estimate is not new actual spend, and local response replay makes no API calls. Missing attempts prevent a complete routed-charge estimate. Specialist deployment cost, total-system dollar cost/savings and production latency stay `null`; **no total-system savings claim** is permitted.

## Commands and authorization

Dry-run needs no credentials and performs no inference. Choose a fresh output directory:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m baseline.general dry-run --output artifacts/exp006-dry-run-new
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
```

After explicit user approval of the paid run, frozen protocol and numeric **$4.00 cap**, the command would be:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m baseline.general live \
  --output artifacts/exp006-gpt6-luna-validation-v1 \
  --authorize-live \
  --max-spend-usd 4.00 \
  --approve-protocol-sha256 d7f824ee761ca90d4dc3a848dd19e3928475c799d6713e03e336dc2a80c9ca68 \
  --acknowledge-pricing-date 2026-09-25
```

**Do not execute that command in this preparation session.** CLI and execution engine both require authorization; possessing a key or seeing this example is not authorization. The only required credential variable is `OPENAI_API_KEY`; `OPENAI_PROJECT_ID` is optional for explicit billing-project selection. Configure credentials securely in the local environment, never in chat or tracked files. This session does not read credential values. The pricing acknowledgement must match the frozen date; live execution rejects verification older than seven days. Recheck official prices before approving a later run and update/review the protocol if necessary. No model may be silently substituted.

To resume an approved interrupted run, use the same command, cap, protocol and artifact directory; successful/terminal responses are not resubmitted. To recompute quality/accounting from a saved live run without credentials or API calls:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m baseline.general evaluate --output artifacts/exp006-gpt6-luna-validation-v1
```

Offline evaluation checks the durable reservation ledger as well as response hashes. Run artifacts with incomplete or fatal states remain evidence; investigate recorded errors without deleting difficult cases or changing the frozen prompt.

## Preparation verification

Synthetic tests cover row/label alignment; request/prompt/schema hashing; frozen protocol drift; resume reuse; bounded failures/retries; refusals/incomplete/invalid responses; interrupted reservations; missing/corrupt cache/ledger files; numeric cap/explicit approval guards; cached/write/reasoning token arithmetic; full-denominator combined metrics; and no-inference CLI behavior. A network/credential guard is active in CLI tests. **243 tests passed**, including 144 new synthetic tests. See [verification.json](verification.json) for test totals and dry-run integrity checks. The existing scientific/model dependency pins are unchanged; the HTTP transport uses Python's standard library, with no new service infrastructure.

During implementation, synthetic review exposed malformed-body handling, missing cached-response evidence, duplicate cache keys, drifted-pricing accounting, and read-only ledger verification gaps. These were fixed and covered by regression tests. They were implementation defects in synthetic tests, not failed or discarded paid experiments. No live integration test, model response, fallback score, spend observation above zero, or cost-saving result exists yet. `docs/RESULTS.md` is unchanged.
